title: Domain-Generalization to Improve Learning in Meta-Learning Algorithms
main_claims: DGS-MAML integrates gradient matching (via SAGM's surrogate gap) into the MAML bi-level optimization framework to achieve better generalisation and faster convergence than SharpMAML.
DGS-MAML achieves a convergence rate of O(1/T), improving over SharpMAML's O(1/sqrt(T)), while not increasing per-iteration cost.
Adding the delta hyperparameter from domain generalisation to the PAC-Bayes bound further tightens the generalisation error compared to SharpMAML.
methodology: The authors combine SAGM's gradient matching objective (minimising empirical loss, perturbed loss, and surrogate gap angle) with the bi-level MAML structure. Convergence analysis for single-level SAGM is derived (new contribution, as original SAGM paper had none), then extended to bi-level DGS-MAML with stochastic gradient variance assumptions. PAC-Bayes bound is derived following SharpMAML's framework with an added delta term. Experiments are conducted on Mini-Imagenet, Omniglot, DoubleMNIST, and TripleMNIST using 5-way/10-way 1-shot and 5-shot settings.
key_results: DGS-MAML achieves 5-way 1-shot accuracy of 0.4665 (delta=2.0) vs. SharpMAML 0.4509 on Mini-Imagenet, a +1.56% improvement over the best SharpMAML configuration.
DGS-MAML achieves convergence rate O(1/T) vs. SharpMAML O(1/sqrt(T)), a qualitative improvement in convergence speed.
Runtime per epoch for DGS-MAML is 60-70 seconds, comparable to SharpMAML (60-65 seconds), confirming negligible computational overhead.
limitations: Fine-tuning delta is crucial for best accuracy, and the authors lack a method for automatic delta selection, requiring numerical grid search.
The convergence analysis uses bounded stochastic gradient and Lipschitz assumptions that are idealised for real deep networks.
Experiments are on few-shot classification tasks only; OOD robustness under distributional shift (e.g., corruptions) is not evaluated.
relevance_to_rq: This paper is only tangentially relevant. It applies SAM-derived flatness objectives in meta-learning, not the discriminative OOD generalisation setting of the RQ. The connection to CIFAR-C benchmarks, CKA representation stability, and the SAM vs. SWA comparison is absent.
